title: The wave--Klein--Gordon Lorentz null numerator cancels the nonzero-mode phase divisor

null_cancellation.phase: For p nonzero, omega(k)=sqrt(M^2+|k|^2) and Phi=|p|+omega(k)-omega(k+p)
null_cancellation.null_numerator: N0=|p| omega(k)-p dot k is the Lorentz wave--Klein--Gordon null numerator on the declared sign branch
null_cancellation.upper_order: The quotient is bounded by |p|+omega(k), so the null-form homological multiplier loses at most one spatial derivative
null_cancellation.sharpness: For p=(1,0,0) and k=(K,0,0), N0/Phi is asymptotic to K; no same-tier bound holds for the unnormalized numerator
null_cancellation.ceiling: This is an exact scalar-symbol result for one sign branch, not a derivation of that numerator from K1413's lifted current or a global PDE estimate
